Green flag
GREEN flag
noun (Gen-Z slang)
Coined as the opposite of red flag on Twitter and TikTok c. 2020–2021. The green flag already meant "go" or "all clear" in railway signalling and in motor racing, where it starts or restarts a race. In the slang a green flag is a sign that a person is kind, trustworthy, and worth pursuing, often posted with a green emoji.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang a green flag is a good sign in a person: he texts back when he says he will, she is kind to her little brother, he respects your parents, she says sorry without being made to. It is the slang’s attempt at a list of virtues. The Christian observation: Scripture is full of green flags, and it gives them a name — fruit. "Every good tree bringeth forth good fruit" (Mat 7:17), and the fruit is listed: "love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance" (Gal 5:22–23). Paul’s list of things to think on is a green-flag list for a whole life: "whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure" (Php 4:8). The slang is right to look for character rather than looks alone, for "the LORD looketh on the heart" (1Sa 16:7). But its green flags tend to be manners and moods — he remembers my coffee order — and the greenest flag of all is missing from most lists: the fear of the Lord. "Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised" (Pro 31:30), and the same is true of a man. A father tells his daughter: notice the boy who is kind; then ask whether he is kind because he is pleasant or because he belongs to Christ, for the first fades and the second grows. He tells his son: be the green flag before you go looking for one.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (c. 2020–present, opposite of red flag) for a good sign in a person — the slang’s list of virtues, which Scripture calls fruit and crowns with the fear of the Lord.

expand to see more

GREEN FLAG, n. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2020–present; opposite of red flag) A trait or habit that signals a person is kind, trustworthy, and worth pursuing as a friend or partner. "He asked my dad first. Green flag."

Posted as a list ("green flags in a girl") or as a green emoji in the comments; green-flag energy, a generally trustworthy manner.

Older senses: the "go" or "all clear" signal on railways; the starting flag in motor racing.

Webster (1828), root word green: “GREEN, adjective 1. Properly, growing, flourishing, as plants; hence, of the color of herbage and plants when growing, a color composed of blue and yellow rays, one of blue and yellow rays, one of the original prismatic colors; verdant. 2. New; fresh; recent; as a green wound. The greenest usurpation. 3. Fresh; flourishing; undecayed;”

Decode for parents: your teen is looking for virtue and calling it a green flag; help him put the fear of the Lord at the top of the list.

Key Scripture

Mat 7:17 — "Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit."

Gal 5:22 — "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,"

Gal 5:23 — "Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law."

Php 4:8 — "Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things."

Pro 31:30 — "Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised."

Modern Corruption

Green flag rightly hunts for character, but its list runs to manners and moods and usually leaves off the one mark Scripture puts first, the fear of the Lord.

expand to see more

This is one of the slang’s better instincts. A generation trained by dating apps to sort by photographs is, in the green-flag lists, trying to sort by character: does he keep his word, is she gentle, do they treat the weak well? Scripture commends the question. Samuel was told, "Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature" (1Sa 16:7), and the virtues of Galatians 5 are exactly the things a spouse lives with for fifty years.

The trouble is the source of the list. Feed-made green flags are often courtesies a clever unbeliever can perform for months: he remembers your birthday, she likes your friends. Good fruit grows from a good tree (Mat 7:17), and the root of that tree is the fear of the Lord (Pro 31:30). Teach your children to look for the green flags that cannot be faked for long — a man in the Word, a woman at prayer, both under the oversight of a faithful church — and to become them first.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English grene (growing, verdant) → railway and racing "go" signal → c. 2020: the opposite of red flag, a good sign in a person.

expand to see more

Old English grene — green, growing, related to grow and grass

19th c. railway signalling: green for "all clear"

20th c. motor racing: the green flag starts the race

c. 2020–2021 TikTok and Twitter: green flag coined against red flag

Now: lists of virtues looked for in a friend or partner

Usage

""He apologised to his little sister without anyone making him. Major green flag.""

"Scripture calls green flags fruit, and lists them (Gal 5:22)."

"The greenest flag is the fear of the Lord (Pro 31:30)."
